Subject: Field appliance - offline update options / proof-of-origin question

Hi Evelyn / Jonas,

We're preparing the next maintenance window for our fleet of 12 field appliances (air-gapped). Attached is a short CSV of current model + serials and the onsite engineer list (inventory.csv). Before we lock the window, we need clarity on two things:

1) Proof of origin: we require cryptographic proof that images/bundles you deliver were produced by Redwood and have not been tampered with en route. We currently accept SHA256 manifests signed by the vendor root key.

2) Offload workflow: our ops team performs physical offload (encrypted SSD/USB) and needs a clear verification + rollback flow to present to compliance.

Can you outline the minimum evidence chain and an example cutover checklist we can present to our auditors? Also let us know whether Redwood can sign bundles with a customer-specific intermediate cert (we prefer per-customer trust anchors).

Thanks,
Aaron Lopez
Delta Manufacturing - Field Ops
attachments: inventory.csv (csv)
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Field appliance - offline update options / proof-of-origin question

Thanks Aaron — good questions. I put together a concise approach below and attached a short preliminary checklist (prelim-checklist.pdf) you can hand to auditors and site techs. High level:

- Bundle signing and provenance
  * We produce release bundles containing the image tarball, a manifest.json (SHA256 checksums for each component), and a detached signature manifest.sig produced by Redwood's HSM-backed signing service.
  * For air-gapped customers we support:
    - Redwood-signed bundles (default) where Redwood retains the CA private key in an HSM, or
    - Customer-intermediate: we can generate a signing intermediate and deliver a CSR for you to sign with your root CA. The intermediate's private key stays in our HSM, and we publish the intermediate cert to the bundle. This gives you a dedicated trust anchor while keeping key material protected.

- Delivery & offload
  * Deliverable package: <product>-<version>-<site>-<timestamp>.tar.gz + manifest + manifest.sig + human-readable checklist (PDF).
  * Transport: encrypted SSD shipped physically or transferred to your secure courier. We recommend AES-256 encrypted container with per-shipment key handed to the site tech via OOB channel.

- Onsite verification steps (minimum evidence chain)
  1) Verify checksum: sha256sum on the tar.gz and compare to manifest.
  2) Verify signature: use our published intermediate/root cert to verify manifest.sig (we provide a simple verify.sh you can run).
  3) Capture a signed acceptance form with serial numbers of target appliances and a timestamped photo of the SSD label (for chain-of-custody).

- Rollback and fail-safe
  * Each appliance keeps the previous image in a separate partition by default. Our agent will not apply the new image until a verification hook returns success. If verification fails, the agent leaves the device on the active partition and reports a non-destructive failure.
  * We provide a tested rollback script (attached in a later message) and a canary plan: deploy to 2-3 devices first, hold for 24 hours and run smoke tests.

Questions for you:
- Do you have a preference on signing model (Redwood HSM vs customer-signed intermediate)?
- What is your preferred OOB key delivery channel to the field techs (SMS + 2FA, secure messenger, courier envelope)?

If OK I will loop in Jonas for the low-level verification commands and send a draft mutual action plan (MAP) that includes roles, time windows, and acceptance criteria.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
attachments: prelim-checklist.pdf
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Eve / Aaron — quick technical clarifications and a recommended verification snippet. I'm pasting the relevant bit of Eve's note inline for context.

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 11:02 AM Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com> wrote:
> We produce release bundles containing the image tarball, a manifest.json (SHA256 checksums for each component), and a detached signature manifest.sig produced by Redwood's HSM-backed signing service.

Recommended low-level verification (example commands):
1) sha256sum -c manifest.sha256  # abort if any mismatch
2) openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json  # returns OK or FAIL
3) tar -tzf bundle.tar.gz --wildcards '*/meta/*' | head -n 20  # confirm expected layout

Notes on signing models:
- Customer intermediate: we can embed the intermediate cert and include an OCSP stapled response for freshness if you maintain an OCSP responder. Without OCSP the cert chain is still valid but auditors often ask for freshness evidence.
- If you want absolute control over the signing key material, we can provide a signing appliance package that runs in your air-gapped environment. That increases operational burden on your side but eliminates any external key custody concerns.

Rollback script (sketch): rollback-script.sh --target <serial> --verify-only | --execute
- Pre-check: ensure backup partition integrity and free space
- If execute: flip bootloader pointer, reboot, watch heartbeats for 10 mins, otherwise flip back

I'll attach a hardened version of the rollback script in the MAP if you want to run canary tests in staging.

-Jonas

From: Aaron Lopez <aaron.lopez@deltamfg.com>

Subject: Re: Field appliance - offline update options / proof-of-origin question

Evelyn / Jonas — this is very helpful, thanks. A few follow-ups from our compliance team:

- We prefer the customer-intermediate model so Delta remains the root trust, but we want Redwood to hold the intermediate private key in an HSM rather than a raw file. That matches your second bullet above.
- For OOB key delivery to field techs, we use sealed courier envelopes for the initial handoff and a phone-based 2FA code for subsequent local decrypts. Works well with AES-256 containers.
- We need the MAP and a signed manifest example that our auditors can replay locally. Could you also include exact openssl commands and an example public.pem we can pin for the audit?

Finally — what is Redwood's recommended acceptance window for canary devices? Our initial thought is 24 hours with smoke tests (connectivity + model sanity + disk integrity). Does that match your expectations?

Thanks,
Aaron
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Lopez <aaron.lopez@deltamfg.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Field appliance - MAP, sample manifest & next steps

Aaron — thanks, we can do that. Attached is a draft MAP (MAP-Delta-20260521.pdf) and a sample manifest.sig (manifest.sig) and the example public.pem you can pin for the audit. Summary below (action items and timeline):

1) Signing model: customer-root with Redwood-issued intermediate stored in Redwood HSM. Deliverables: CSR for your root CA (we'll generate CSR and intermediate cert), sample public.pem, sample manifest.sig for a release candidate.

2) Deliverables and evidence artifacts (what we will hand over):
   - bundle: delta-appliance-2.1.3-nyc-20260521.tar.gz
   - manifest.sha256 + manifest.json
   - manifest.sig (detached, HSM-signed)
   - MAP-Delta-20260521.pdf (runbook + acceptance criteria)
   - evidence template (signed acceptance form + photo checklist)

3) Canary & rollout plan:
   - Canary: 3 appliances in non-critical site for 24 hours, run the smoke suite (connectivity, model health, disk checks).
   - Stage: 10 appliances for 48 hours.
   - Full: remaining fleet after stage approval.
   - Rollback: instant keep-alive monitor; if >1 critical failure in canary (configurable threshold), automatic halt and manual review.

4) Verification commands (exact examples we will include in the MAP):
   - sha256sum -c manifest.sha256
   - openssl dgst -sha256 -verify public.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json
   - ./rollback-script.sh --target <serial> --verify-only

5) Compliance notes:
   - We will timestamp-sign manifests and include the intermediate cert chain; we can include an OCSP stapled response on request.
   - All package builds will be reproducible; we will provide build logs and the CI artifact IDs for traceability.

Next steps:
- Aaron: confirm acceptance of the MAP PDF and signing model (customer-root w/ Redwood HSM intermediate).
- Delta: provide root CA signing window or a copy of the signed intermediate cert once issued.
- Redwood: prepare the CSR and sample manifest + public.pem and a hardened rollback script; schedule a 2-hour conference call to walk the on-site team through verification steps the week of 2026-06-01.

Attaching: MAP-Delta-20260521.pdf, manifest.sig

Best regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
